notes.title: SOLAS 128 and the CRT7 Demo are in the Cerebral Puzzle Showcase!
notes.content:
Hi all, Tom here!

Today is the official announcement of the 2023 Cerebral Puzzle Showcase which means I can say that both SOLAS 128 and CRT7 were selected to take part! I'm delighted and flattered to have both my games in this event, alongside 200+ other incredible thinky games.

SOLAS 128 will be discounted by 60% for the event (it's deepest discount ever) and CRT7 will be one of only 5 new demos debuting during the event, too!

Whether you like wordless exploration of an ancient interconnected neon machine, or exploring a dark basement full of weird corrupted retro machines, there is sure to be something you like here. Not only that, but it seems like the two games might even be connected somehow?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/58d0e115d76de0b6c760bfed75ec2217b665b71c.gif[/img]

If you try either game during the showcase: thank you so much! I really hope you have fun!

- Amicable Animal

notes.title: New Game: CRT7 Demo Date Announced
notes.content:
Hi all, Tom here!

I'm delighted to say that I can finally announce a date for the upcoming demo of my new game, CRT7! The demo will be launching 3rd of August! If you're interested, please wishlist it here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2096780/CRT7/


What's more, I've made a special trailer to celebrate the announcement. I really hope you like it:

[previewyoutube=13wSru0sJkI;full][/previewyoutube]
Solve puzzles / Explore the dark / Fix the future

The demo is somewhere between 1 and 3 hours long (depending how good you are at puzzles), and should give you a good idea of what to expect from the full game. A dark basement, mysterious puzzles, and a splintered narrative about obsession, power, and regret. It will also have an embedded guidance/hint system and accessibility options too.

Oh, and you better believe I hid some fun weirdness in there too...

I can't wait to see people playing it! Please bear in mind that this is a one-person solo project so bugs are always likely although I'm doing my best to squash them as we speak. But, as always, please do share the news, tell your friends, and wishlist the game - it's such a huge help!

- Amicable Animal

notes.title: SOLAS 128 Accessibilty Update and 34% Off Sale
notes.content:
Hey all, Tom here!

Big news today, as not only is there a huge SOLAS 128 Accessibility update, but also a sale to celebrate Global Accessibility Awareness Day!

As some of you might be aware, accessibility has been a core part of the design of SOLAS 128 from the start. The coloured glyphs are designed to help those with colour-blindness be able to play the game, for example. But I was aware it wasn't perfect. Since launch we've had fantastic feedback and suggestions from players and accessibility experts, and I've been working on a big update to make the game even more customisable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/04edff6a34c31cef0be16149fd3ec5b2bd881ea4.jpg[/img]

Once updated, players will find a whole new menu of options full of player-requested options like being able to tweak the bloom or colour distortion amount, or even an entirely new input method for those who struggle to hold down buttons. Keyboard input has also been massively improved, to allow more accurate movement with the cursor/WASD keys, and a new hotkeys have been added to skip straight to the next or previous piece you can interact with.

[b] If you're not sure, please do try out the demo/prologue first, as I've updated it as well, to made sure all the same options are available. If you can customise the demo to work for you, you'll be able to customise the full game too![/b]

For a full list of new features/updates see below, but I really hope these updates help!

-Amicable Animal

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[h3]Visual Options (for visual processing accessibility)[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Settings for the bloom/glow effect (original, low, off)
[*] Settings for colour distortion/chromic aberration (original, low, off)
[*] Option for the VHS-style video distortion effects (on, off)
[*] Settings to simplify the game's surrounding border pattern (original, static, solid colour)
[*] Option for the 'flashing' effect in the surrounding pattern (on, off)
[/olist]
[h3]Input Options (for motor accessibility)[/h3]
[olist]
[*] New input type - original input is click & drag, new option removes requirement to hold down a button while dragging. One click to pick up, a second to put down
[*] New optional precision input method - directional keys (d-pad on Switch) will move the cursor locked to the game's tile grid, rather than as a smooth input.
[*] Can either be depressed once per tile, or held down as desired
[*] Analogue/mouse and precision input can be swapped between freely and used at the same time
[*] New selection method - Next/Previous selection option lets players with visual processing issues or motor issues cycle through selectable pieces.
[/olist]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Filters will now check and reactive if necessarily when you change screen
[*] 'Invalid' spaces should appear more obvious now
[*] Lots of other tiny fixes
[/olist]

notes.title: SOLAS 128 Patch Notes - v1.02
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

Today's SOLAS 128 update addresses a couple bugs and strange behaviors reported since the game launched.  If you've been enjoying the game please be sure to leave a review here on Steam, it's a great way to continue to support the game.   You can find the full details of the patch below.  



[b]SOLAS 128  v1.02 Changelog[/b]
[list]
[*] Penultimate cutscene should no longer softlock the game if the mirrors have already been removed
[*] Players should no longer be able to 'fast forward' through the game outro
[*] Flip mirrors should be much less likely to change orientation when the game is saving, so older areas shouldn't need to be rewired
[*] Pulse doors should no longer get out of sync if they are transitioning during a save/screen move/quit action
[*] A pulse button in the red area should no longer affect a pulse door in the green area (starting from a new save required)
[*] Filter emitters should now act as walls for the pulses, rather than mirrors – pulses can no longer 'escape' the world through them later in the game and cause issues. 
[/list]

notes.title: The Reviews Are In!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

SOLAS 128 has been out for just over a week now, and we're incredibly pleased to hear everyone enjoying the game! We picked some of our favorites reviews to share with you here.

***

"This is something truly very special. A laser-bouncing puzzle game that takes the format not to the next level, but to a whole other cosmic order... I kept hearing the word “masterpiece” go through my brain as I was playing it. Not a word I like to use, but still, it kept whispering itself to me."
- [url=https://buried-treasure.org/2021/02/solas-128/]Buried Treasure[/url]

***

"When Johnathan Blow's [i]The Witness[/i] came out in 2016, I immediately fell in love... No other game has scratched that particular puzzling itch for me... until [i][b]SOLAS 128[/b][/i]"
-[url=https://www.godisageek.com/reviews/solas-128-review/]8.5/10, God is a Geek[/url]

***

"...if you like puzzle games about reflecting light beams, you would be hard-pressed to find a bigger, more satisfying example than[i][b] SOLAS 128.[/b][/i]"
 - [url=https://toucharcade.com/2021/02/01/switcharcade-round-up-mini-views-featuring-gods-will-fall-plus-turrican-flashback-and-todays-other-releases-and-sales/]4/5, Touch Arcade[/url]

***

"...the steady beat of the synthwave music keeps the brain flowing along in a puzzley trance." 
- [url=https://hardcoregamer.com/2021/01/25/review-solas-128/395951/]3.5./5, Hardcore Gamer[/url]

***

Thank you again for such a warm and wonderful launch. If you've already picked up SOLAS 128 we'd love to hear your thoughts in a Steam review or in a discussion on the [url=https://discord.gg/TwSEKh7zyn][b]SOLAS 128 Discord. [/b][/url]
